en: About 1,300 Earths could fit inside Jupiter, making it the largest planet in our solar system.
The Moon is approximately 384,400 kilometers away from Earth, meaning about 30 Earths could fit between them.
On the Mohs hardness scale, talc has a rating of 1, while diamond is the hardest mineral with a 10.
The highest officially recorded air temperature on Earth was 56.7 degrees Celsius in Death Valley, California, in 1913.
About 97 percent of Earth's water is salty ocean water, leaving only 3 percent as fresh water.
Proxima Centauri is the closest star to our solar system, located about 4.24 light-years or 40 trillion kilometers away.
Clay soil particles are the smallest at less than 0.002 millimeters, while sand particles measure up to 2 millimeters.
The 1960 Valdivia earthquake in Chile is the most powerful ever recorded, measuring a massive 9.5 magnitude.
Neptune is located about 4.5 billion kilometers from the Sun, making it roughly 30 times farther than Earth.
Super Typhoon Haiyan, one of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded, had maximum sustained winds reaching 315 kilometers per hour.
The Moon's diameter is 3,474 kilometers, which is about one-quarter the size of Earth's 12,742-kilometer diameter.
Scientists have identified over 5,800 distinct minerals on Earth, but feldspar minerals alone make up nearly half the crust.
